newsitem.title: ESTONIA: LEKS PLANS SHARE ISSUE PRICE OF 1.9 KROONS.
newsitem.headline: LEKS PLANS SHARE ISSUE PRICE OF 1.9 KROONS.

text.p: Leading Estonian insurance company Leks said it is planning to issue shares on the secondary list of the stock market at a nominal price of 1.9 kroons per share for a total issue of four million kroons.
"The share emission will start in the last week of this month and will be handled by Talinvest," Leks chairman Raul Kastan told Reuters in a recent interview.
"At first all this emission will be four million Estonian kroons," he said.
"This emission will be 1.9 (kroons) at nominal value," he added.
He said the prospectus for the issue was almost ready and that the shares would start on the secondary list of the market with computer maker Pennu and Evea Pank.
"Our owners need this (a stock market quote). After this they will know the commercial price of this stock," he added.
"We are the first insurance company to go to the market and it is good from the market's point of view as well," he added.
Kastan was optimistic over the company's growth prospects, saying he was expecting growth of some 40 percent in 1997.
He said the company currently had 15 percent of the non-life insurance market.
Kastan said the company may also consider an expansion into the Lithuanian and Latvian markets.
A possible need to raise extra capital before moving into the neighbouring markets was one of their reasons for seeking a listing on the market.
"Maybe when we go to the Latvian and Lithuanian market we may need more capital," he said.
Kastan said that the key growth areas for Leks were property insurance, company insurance and private insurance.
